title: Type
summary: A type classifies expressions and states which constructions may be formed with them.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared type theory context is fixed.

content.plain: A type classifies expressions and states which constructions may be formed with them.
content.exact: Judgments such as a:A assert that term a has type A; formation, introduction, elimination, and computation rules define each type constructor.
content.example: n:ℕ records that n is a natural-number term.
content.caveat: Types are not always sets, though some models interpret them set-theoretically.
